done_when: Forge's Codex trust check accepts a project inside a trusted folder whenever Codex itself trusts it, and asks only when Codex would ask

known.title: Trust lookup can authorize turns that Codex treats as untrusted
Not done: Forge's Codex trust check accepts a project inside a trusted folder whenever Codex trusts it, and asks only when Codex would ask
Standard: each commit leaves the build working

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security. `Path(path).resolve()` treats distinct Codex trust keys as the same key. On Windows, a valid TOML entry using `C:/work/app` becomes the same path as `C:\work\app` in Forge, but Codex only lowercases trust keys; it does not convert separators. Forge can therefore start a turn while Codex considers the project untrusted and skips its hooks. The new test writes keys with `as_posix()`, so it would endorse this mismatch on Windows. Codex's lookup is in [its pinned source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.159.2/codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs#L1302-L1338).
findings.title: Trust lookup can authorize turns that Codex treats as untrusted

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. Codex checks its configured project root between the current directory and Git repository root, but this code checks only the checkout and main checkout. With `project_root_markers = ["workspace.marker"]`, a marker and trusted entry on a containing workspace folder, and a Git project below it, Codex trusts the project while Forge asks for trust. The test covers only Codex's default `.git` marker. See Codex's [decision order](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.159.2/codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs#L984-L1025) and [project-root discovery](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.159.2/codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs#L1197-L1210).

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Gate. The standard says, "Commit messages are short plain English, and each commit leaves the build working, so any commit can be reverted alone." This changed refusal now prints `Next: open Codex here...`, while the unchanged `tests/test_codex_setup.py:170-171` asserts the entire refusal ends with `Next: forge doctor`. That test necessarily fails in the repository's full pytest suite.
